stem: Zubin shares one idli equally. He compares the unit fractions $1/5$ and $1/10$ from that whole.

options.text: $1/5$ is greater than $1/10$ because fewer equal shares make each share larger.
$1/10$ is greater than $1/5$ because 10 is greater than 5.
$1/5$ and $1/10$ are equal because each numerator is 1.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that uses the size of a unit fraction.

part_answers.answer: For the same whole, a larger denominator makes each equal share smaller, so 1/5 is greater than 1/10.

teacher.key_rationale: With the same whole, more equal shares make each unit fraction smaller. Comparing denominators as if larger means greater reverses the size rule. Matching numerators alone is a surface feature.
